value.why: Sweet and bridge: sweet Layon Chenin tastes of quince and baked apple, and its acidity keeps the brown sugar glaze fresh.
value.sayIt: With the baked apple, a sweet Chenin from the Loire: quince, honey and baked apple, with a bright finish.

classic.why: Sweet and acid: a moelleux Vouvray is as sweet as the glaze, and Chenin acidity lifts the crème fraîche.
classic.sayIt: For something special, the Huet Moelleux from Vouvray: honeyed, golden Chenin that tastes like the apple itself.

splurge.why: Bridge and sweet: late harvest Gewürztraminer carries cinnamon spice and ripe fruit that echo the crumble and glaze.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, a Trimbach late harvest Gewürztraminer from Alsace: rich, spiced, and perfect with warm apple and cinnamon.

half.why: Sweet and bridge: a demi-sec Chenin half is just sweet enough for the glaze and tastes of apple and honey.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Huet Le Mont demi-sec: gently sweet Vouvray, apple and honey, just right for breakfast.

value.why: Weight and tannin: Grenache-led Gigondas has ripe fruit for the filet and soft tannins that suit a morning course.
value.sayIt: With the filet, a Gigondas from the Southern Rhône: ripe red fruit, a little spice, and soft enough for breakfast.

classic.why: Weight and fat: Châteauneuf has the body for beef and garlic spinach, with spice that flatters the crisp rösti.
classic.sayIt: If you would like a bottle, the Pegau Châteauneuf-du-Pape: generous, spicy and warm, beautiful with the filet.

splurge.why: Tannin and weight: an older Beaucastel has softened tannins and savory depth that meet tender beef without overpowering it.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, a mature Château de Beaucastel: savory, silky Châteauneuf with years of age, lovely with the filet.

half.why: Weight: a half of Gigondas gives Grenache fruit and body for the filet without committing to a full bottle.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Raspail-Ay Gigondas: ripe and spicy, just enough for two with the filet.

value.why: Fat and acid: Bourgogne Chardonnay has the texture for lobster and buttery sauce, and fresh acidity after the nduja.
value.sayIt: With the lobster, a white Burgundy from Fichet: creamy and bright, lovely with the butter and a little spice.

classic.why: Fat and weight: Meursault richness matches lobster and barbecue butter, and its freshness keeps the white bean stew lively.
classic.sayIt: The Dupont-Fahn Meursault is rich and nutty, exactly what lobster and that peppery butter sauce want.

splurge.why: Fat and bridge: a Leflaive Meursault Premier Cru brings nutty, toasty depth that meets roasted lobster and smoky nduja.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Leflaive Meursault Premier Cru: layered, toasty white Burgundy, a real match for lobster.

half.why: Fat: a half of village Meursault gives the same buttery richness for lobster in a smaller pour.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Jadot Meursault: rich, round white Burgundy, perfect for the lobster course.

value.why: Fat and acid: Bourgogne Pinot Noir has bright acidity for rich duck and red fruit for the glazed peaches.
value.sayIt: With the duck, a red Burgundy from Faiveley: bright cherry fruit and fresh acidity, classic with duck.

classic.why: Fat and bridge: a mature Nuits-Saint-Georges Premier Cru brings earthy depth for duck and fruit for the cane syrup peaches.
classic.sayIt: The Gouges Nuits-Saint-Georges Les Pruliers has some age now: earthy, dark cherry, and gorgeous with duck.

splurge.why: Fat and tannin: a fifteen year old Echézeaux has silky tannin and layered fruit that rise to the richest duck.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Grivot Echézeaux, a Grand Cru red Burgundy with age: silky, perfumed and wonderful with duck.

half.why: Fat and acid: a half of Gouges Nuits-Saint-Georges gives Pinot acidity for duck in a two glass pour.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Henri Gouges Nuits-Saint-Georges: savory red Burgundy, just right with the duck.

value.why: Sweet and acid: late harvest Moscadello is sweeter than the curds, with orange blossom freshness for lemon and coconut.
value.sayIt: With the trifle, a late harvest Moscadello from Montalcino: honeyed, floral, and bright enough for the lemon curd.

classic.why: Bridge and acid: Cabernet Franc ice wine has red berry fruit for the blackberry and the acidity to stay fresh.
classic.sayIt: For something unusual, an Inniskillin red ice wine from Niagara: sweet berries and bright acidity, made for this trifle.

splurge.why: Bridge and sweet: Quintarelli Recioto is sweet red wine from dried grapes, its dark berry fruit echoing the blackberry curd.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Quintarelli Recioto: a sweet red from the Veneto, dark berries and spice, stunning with blackberry.

half.why: Sweet and acid: a Goldkapsel Auslese half has the sweetness and piercing acidity a lemon and blackberry dessert needs.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Dönhoff Auslese from the Nahe: honeyed, racy Riesling that loves the lemon curd.

value.why: Sweet and acid: a Goldkapsel Spätlese is sweet enough for the coulis, and its acidity cuts mascarpone and brioche.
value.sayIt: With the French toast, a Mosel Riesling Spätlese from Dr. Hermann: sweet, bright and juicy with the raspberries.

classic.why: Bridge and fat: demi-sec rosé Champagne has red berry fruit for the raspberries and bubbles to lift the mascarpone mousse.
classic.sayIt: For a festive brunch, Moët Nectar Impérial Rosé: a gently sweet pink Champagne, raspberries and cream in a glass.

splurge.why: Sweet and fat: Yquem has the richness and sweetness for mascarpone and coulis, with acidity to keep brioche light.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, a half-bottle of Château d’Yquem: the most famous sweet wine in the world, honeyed and luminous.

half.why: Sweet and fat: a demi-sec Champagne half matches the sweetness, and its bubbles scrub the mascarpone from the palate.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Laurent-Perrier Harmony demi-sec: lightly sweet Champagne, perfect with brioche and berries.

value.why: Bridge and sweet: a Late Bottled Vintage Port brings dark fruit and cocoa notes for chocolate and chicory coffee.
value.sayIt: With the coffee cake, a Late Bottled Vintage Port from Feist: dark fruit and chocolate notes, lovely with the chicory.

classic.why: Bridge and acid: Malvasia Madeira tastes of coffee, caramel and orange peel, and its acidity matches the spiced citrus glaze.
classic.sayIt: For something special, a single cask Malvasia Madeira: coffee, caramel and orange, just like a café brûlot.

splurge.why: Sweet and tannin: a mature vintage Port has softened tannin and dried fruit depth for bittersweet chocolate and pecans.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, a Niepoort vintage Port with real age: mellow, dried fruit and spice, gorgeous with chocolate.

half.why: Bridge and sweet: a Colheita half is single vintage tawny Port, its nutty caramel meeting pecans and coffee.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Niepoort Colheita: an aged tawny Port, nutty and caramel, wonderful with the pecans.

value.why: Acid and fat: dry Vouvray has the texture for buttery barbecue sauce and the acidity for pickled collards.
value.sayIt: With the barbecue oysters, a dry Chenin from Huet: textured, bright and great with the butter and pepper.

classic.why: Fat and salt: Grand Cru grower Champagne cuts the buttery sauce and the fried saltine crumble, and loves the oyster brine.
classic.sayIt: For a bottle of bubbles, the Pierre Paillard Grand Cru Extra Brut: very dry, crisp and perfect with fried and buttery.

splurge.why: Weight and fat: all Pinot Noir Bollinger has the body to stand up to barbecue butter and peppery sauce.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Bollinger PN: all Pinot Noir Champagne, full and powerful enough for barbecue oysters.

half.why: Acid: a half of dry Vouvray brings Chenin acidity for the pickled greens and enough body for the sauce.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Huet Le Haut Lieu Sec: dry, crisp Chenin, made for these oysters.

value.why: Acid and bridge: dry Provence rosé has the acidity for raw tomato and the delicacy for creamy burrata.
value.sayIt: With the tomatoes, Whispering Angel from Provence: pale, dry and refreshing, exactly right for a summer tomato.

classic.why: Acid and weight: Bandol rosé has more body and savory depth, standing up to smoked tomato water and okra.
classic.sayIt: For a step up, the Tempier Bandol rosé: dry, savory and serious, one of the great rosés of France.

splurge.why: Acid and bridge: Cotat Pinot Noir rosé from Chavignol brings chalky acidity and red fruit for heirloom tomatoes.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Pascal Cotat rosé from Sancerre country: rare, mineral and beautiful with the tomatoes.

value.why: Fat and acid: Pouilly-Fuissé has round Chardonnay richness for brown butter and acidity for the vinaigrette.
value.sayIt: With the crab claws, a Pouilly-Fuissé from Roc des Boutires: round, fresh Chardonnay that loves brown butter.

classic.why: Fat and acid: Saint-Aubin Premier Cru brings nutty richness for brown butter and a chalky snap for sweet crab.
classic.sayIt: The Paul Pillot Saint-Aubin Le Charmois is nutty and bright, made for brown butter and crab.

splurge.why: Fat and bridge: Puligny-Montrachet has toasty, nutty depth that mirrors brown butter and lifts fines herbes.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Carillon Puligny-Montrachet: elegant white Burgundy, toasty and fresh, beautiful with the claws.

half.why: Fat and acid: a half of Bourgogne Blanc gives Chardonnay texture for brown butter in a lighter pour.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Matrot Bourgogne Blanc: fresh white Burgundy, just right with crab claws.

value.why: Salt and acid: Muscadet is bone dry with saline acidity that mirrors oyster brine and the mignonette vinegar.
value.sayIt: With raw oysters, a Muscadet from Pépière: bone dry, salty and crisp, the classic oyster wine.

classic.why: Acid and salt: chalky Blanc de Blancs Extra Brut matches brine and vinegar, and its bubbles calm the chili.
classic.sayIt: For bubbles with oysters, the Larmandier-Bernier Longitude: all Chardonnay, very dry and chalky, perfect with brine.

splurge.why: Acid and salt: Grand Cru Chablis has steely acidity and a shell-like minerality that sings with raw oysters.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Dauvissat Chablis Les Preuses: Grand Cru Chablis with age, mineral and precise with oysters.

half.why: Acid and salt: a half of Blanc de Blancs Extra Brut gives dry, chalky bubbles for a dozen oysters.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Veuve Fourny Blanc de Blancs: bone dry Champagne, ideal with a plate of oysters.

value.why: Bridge and fat: English sparkling rosé has red fruit for raw beef and bubbles that cut crème fraîche and crisp potato.
value.sayIt: With the tartare, a sparkling rosé from Chapel Down in England: red berries and fine bubbles, lovely with raw beef.

classic.why: Bridge and fat: Pinot-led rosé Champagne has the red fruit for beef and the freshness for yolk and bottarga.
classic.sayIt: The Chartogne-Taillet rosé is a grower Champagne with real red fruit, beautiful with the tartare.

splurge.why: Weight and bridge: vintage rosé Champagne with age has the depth for raw beef and savory bottarga.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Billecart-Salmon Cuvée Elisabeth Salmon Rosé: elegant vintage pink Champagne, superb with tartare.

half.why: Bridge: a half of rosé Champagne brings red fruit and bubbles for a starter portion of tartare.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Veuve Fourny rosé Champagne: bright and dry, a lovely start with the tartare.

value.why: Bridge and weight: Savennières Chenin is dry, waxy and nutty, with the body for turtle soup and a note that meets sherry.
value.sayIt: With the turtle soup, a dry Savennières from the Loire: rich, nutty Chenin that picks up the sherry.

classic.why: Bridge and salt: Bollinger has a rich, nutty, toasty style that echoes the aged sherry and lifts the soup.
classic.sayIt: For a bottle of Champagne, Bollinger Special Cuvée: rich and toasty, a beautiful match for turtle soup and sherry.

splurge.why: Bridge: Vin Jaune ages under a veil of yeast like sherry, so its nutty, savory character mirrors the aged sherry exactly.
splurge.sayIt: For something truly special, Pélican Vin Jaune from the Jura: nutty and savory like fine sherry, made for turtle soup.

half.why: Bridge and salt: Manzanilla is bone dry sherry, so it repeats the sherry in the soup and cuts its richness.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of La Cigarrera Manzanilla: bone dry sherry, a natural partner for a soup finished with sherry.

value.why: Heat and sweet: a feinherb Riesling has a touch of sweetness that cools andouille spice, with acidity for the roux.
value.sayIt: With gumbo, a Mosel Riesling from Stein: just off dry, bright, and it calms the spice beautifully.

classic.why: Heat and acid: JJ Prüm Kabinett is light, lightly sweet and racy, so it soothes spice and refreshes after the roux.
classic.sayIt: For a step up, JJ Prüm Wehlener Sonnenuhr Kabinett: a classic Mosel Riesling, delicate and bright with the gumbo.

splurge.why: Heat and acid: Scharzhofberger Kabinett has electric acidity and gentle sweetness that tame spice and lift seafood.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Egon Müller Scharzhofberger Kabinett: one of the most sought after Rieslings in the world.

half.why: Acid: a half of dry Kamptal Riesling has the acidity for a dark roux and shellfish.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Bründlmayer Heiligenstein Riesling from Austria: dry, bright and great with gumbo.

value.why: Salt and acid: mineral Muscadet matches the smoked oyster dressing and cuts the Grana Padano.
value.sayIt: With the Caesar, a Muscadet from Domaine L’Ecu: crisp, mineral and salty, lovely with the oyster dressing.

classic.why: Salt and acid: old vine Albariño has saline citrus that meets smoked oyster and cheese.
classic.sayIt: For a bottle, Do Ferreiro Cepas Vellas Albariño from Rías Baixas: citrus, sea spray and depth.

splurge.why: Acid and salt: Cotat Sancerre has the acidity and chalky grip to stand up to a bold, savory dressing.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Pascal Cotat Sancerre Les Monts Damnés: a rare, mineral Sauvignon Blanc, superb with the Caesar.

half.why: Acid: a half of Sauvignon Blanc gives crisp citrus for the dressing in a light lunch pour.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Duckhorn Sauvignon Blanc: crisp and citrusy, a nice partner for the Caesar.

value.why: Fat and acid: English sparkling has bright acidity and bubbles that slice through hollandaise and yolk.
value.sayIt: With the Hussarde, Ridgeview Bloomsbury from Sussex: English sparkling wine, crisp and toasty, great with hollandaise.

classic.why: Fat and acid: our very dry house Champagne cuts hollandaise and yolk, and its toastiness suits the coffee-cured bacon.
classic.sayIt: Eggs and Champagne: a bottle of our own Brennan’s Essential by Piper-Heidsieck, very dry, so the hollandaise stays light.

splurge.why: Fat and bridge: Rare is a prestige vintage Champagne whose depth meets bacon and the marchand de vin.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, a bottle of Rare: Piper-Heidsieck’s prestige vintage Champagne, rich and elegant with eggs.

half.why: Fat and acid: a half of Brut Champagne gives two glasses of bubbles to clear rich hollandaise.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Nicolas Feuillatte Brut: crisp Champagne for two, perfect with brunch.

value.why: Bridge and acid: Grüner Veltliner handles artichokes, which upset most wines, and its peppery freshness cuts creamed spinach.
value.sayIt: Artichokes are tricky with wine, but Grüner Veltliner loves them: the Loimer Lois is crisp and peppery.

classic.why: Bridge and weight: old vine Grüner has more texture for Choron sauce and stays friendly with artichoke.
classic.sayIt: For a bottle, Bründlmayer Alte Reben Grüner Veltliner: textured, peppery and lovely with the Sardou.

splurge.why: Weight and bridge: a Smaragd Grüner Veltliner has the richness for creamed spinach and Choron, and still loves artichoke.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Hirtzberger Honivogl Smaragd from the Wachau: a grand, rich Grüner Veltliner.

half.why: Bridge: a half of classic Grüner gives the artichoke-friendly match in a lighter pour.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Bründlmayer Grüner Veltliner: fresh and peppery, a smart match with artichokes.

value.why: Tannin and bridge: Morgon Gamay has low tannin that will not clash with egg, and juicy fruit for braised short rib.
value.sayIt: With the Eggs Owen, a Morgon from Lapierre: juicy, silky Gamay that loves the short rib and the egg.

classic.why: Bridge and fat: Savigny Premier Cru Pinot Noir echoes the red wine braise and stays light enough for hollandaise.
classic.sayIt: The Tollot-Beaut Savigny-lès-Beaune Les Lavières is a red Burgundy that matches the red wine braise.

splurge.why: Weight and bridge: an aged Volnay Premier Cru has silky depth that meets braised short rib and marchand de vin.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Marquis d’Angerville Volnay Clos des Ducs: silky, perfumed red Burgundy with age.

half.why: Bridge: a half of Beaune Premier Cru gives red Burgundy for the braise without too much at brunch.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Bouchard Beaune Clos de la Mousse: gentle red Burgundy, lovely with the short rib.

value.why: Sweet and acid: a Spätlese-feinherb Riesling has a touch of sweetness for maple and acidity for duck fat.
value.sayIt: With the duck and maple, an off dry Mosel Riesling from Stein: bright, juicy and perfect with the syrup.

classic.why: Fat and weight: Alsace Pinot Gris is a classic with foie gras, rich enough for confit and gently spicy.
classic.sayIt: For a bottle, Albert Boxler Pinot Gris from Alsace: rich and spicy, the classic wine for foie gras.

splurge.why: Fat and weight: a Trimbach Reserve Personnelle Pinot Gris has the opulence for foie gras butter and the depth for confit.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Trimbach Pinot Gris Réserve Personnelle: deep, rich Alsace white, made for foie gras.

half.why: Sweet and acid: a demi-sec Chenin half is sweet enough for the mustard maple syrup and bright enough for the duck fat.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Huet Le Mont demi-sec: gently sweet Vouvray, apple and honey, lovely with duck and maple.
half.note: Re-chosen by the repairer, 4 October 2026: the Dr. Hermann Auslese half is the menu wine with its own card, so the bottle list card that repeated it was dropped.

value.why: Heat and acid: chilled Fleurie has juicy fruit and low tannin for Creole sauce and tasso spice.
value.sayIt: With shrimp and grits, a lightly chilled Fleurie, Clos de la Roilette: juicy Gamay, great with tomato and spice.

classic.why: Heat and bridge: Morgon Côte du Py has more depth for smoky tasso and pimento cheese, with tannin soft enough for spice.
classic.sayIt: For a bottle, Jean Foillard Morgon Côte du Py: savory, juicy Gamay that loves the tasso and Creole sauce.

splurge.why: Bridge and fat: Krug Rosé has red fruit and power for shrimp, smoky tasso and fried grit cake.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Krug Rosé: rich, rare pink Champagne, glorious with shrimp and grits.

half.why: Heat: a half of Beaujolais-Villages gives light, fruity red that stays calm with Creole spice.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Jadot Beaujolais-Villages: light and fruity, easy with shrimp and grits.

value.why: Fat and weight: Santa Rita Hills Chardonnay has texture for crab and cauliflower purée and acidity for the fish.
value.sayIt: With the pecan fish, Sandhi Chardonnay from Santa Rita Hills: fresh but creamy, lovely with crab and pecans.

classic.why: Fat and bridge: Napa Chardonnay brings richness for pecan bordelaise and crab, with balance for flaky fish.
classic.sayIt: The Chateau Montelena Chardonnay from Napa is rich and balanced, beautiful with pecans and crab.

splurge.why: Weight and fat: a Kongsgaard Chardonnay with age has the power for pecan bordelaise and lump crab.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Kongsgaard Chardonnay from Napa: rich, layered, and a cult favorite, superb with the pecan fish.

half.why: Fat: a half of Sonoma Chardonnay gives creamy texture for crab and purée in a light pour.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Chalk Hill Chardonnay: creamy and round, a nice match for the pecan fish.

value.why: Fat and acid: Kumeu River Chardonnay has gentle richness for crab and miso butter and citrus for the lemon.
value.sayIt: With the omelette, Kumeu River Chardonnay from New Zealand: fresh, creamy and bright with lemon and crab.

classic.why: Fat and bridge: Mâcon Milly-Lamartine has round fruit that meets sweet corn and a chalky freshness for lemon.
classic.sayIt: For a bottle, the Lafon Mâcon Milly-Lamartine: round, bright white Burgundy, lovely with corn and crab.

splurge.why: Fat and weight: Lafon Meursault Clos de la Baronne has richness for miso butter and the freshness for basil and lemon.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Comtes Lafon Meursault Clos de la Baronne: rich, precise white Burgundy from a great name.

half.why: Acid: a half of Chablis Premier Cru gives citrus and chalk for lemon and crab at brunch.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Louis Michel Chablis Montmains: crisp and mineral, great with crab.

value.why: Tannin and fat: Saint-Estèphe Cabernet has structure for hanger steak and cuts through béarnaise and yolk.
value.sayIt: With the hanger steak, La Chapelle de Meyney from Saint-Estèphe: classic Bordeaux, firm and savory with béarnaise.

classic.why: Tannin and bridge: Rioja Gran Reserva has mellow tannin and savory spice that suit Creole seasoning and smoked potato.
classic.sayIt: For a bottle, La Rioja Alta 904 Gran Reserva: aged Rioja, savory and mellow, lovely with the smoked potato.

splurge.why: Tannin and weight: Grand-Puy-Lacoste with age has firm, resolved Pauillac tannin for beef and béarnaise.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Château Grand-Puy-Lacoste from Pauillac: classic, aged Bordeaux with steak and béarnaise.

half.why: Tannin: a half of Saint-Émilion gives Merlot-led structure for steak at lunch.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Troplong-Mondot from Saint-Émilion: plush Bordeaux, a lovely lunch pour with steak.

value.why: Tannin and fat: Napa Cabernet has ripe fruit and structure for tenderloin and buttery sauce Foyot.
value.sayIt: With the Chateaubriand, Duckhorn Napa Cabernet: ripe, polished and structured, a sure thing with beef.

classic.why: Tannin and weight: Saint-Julien Cabernet has the structure and cedar for a classic French beef course.
classic.sayIt: For a bottle, Château Talbot from Saint-Julien: classic Bordeaux, cedar and blackcurrant, made for Chateaubriand.

splurge.why: Tannin and fat: a mature Pichon Lalande has silky Pauillac tannin and depth for tenderloin and sauce Foyot.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Pichon-Longueville Comtesse de Lalande with age: elegant Pauillac, perfect for a dish for two.

half.why: Tannin: a half of Ridge Estate Cabernet gives structure for beef in a two glass pour.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Ridge Estate Cabernet: structured and savory, just right for two with beef.

value.why: Acid and fat: Chablis has the acidity for preserved lemon and pickled grapes and enough texture for beurre blanc.
value.sayIt: With the redfish, Louis Michel Chablis: crisp, mineral Chardonnay, lovely with the lemon beurre blanc.

classic.why: Fat and acid: Leflaive Mâcon-Verzé has the texture for beurre blanc and citrus for preserved lemon.
classic.sayIt: For a bottle, Domaine Leflaive Mâcon-Verzé: elegant white Burgundy from a great name, made for beurre blanc.

splurge.why: Fat and bridge: Leflaive Puligny-Montrachet has silky richness and citrus that meet beurre blanc and braised leeks.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Domaine Leflaive Puligny-Montrachet: one of the great white Burgundies, silky with the redfish.

half.why: Acid: a half of Chablis Premier Cru gives crisp acidity for lemon beurre blanc.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Louis Michel Chablis Montmains: crisp and chalky with the redfish.

value.why: Salt and bridge: Godello has saline, almond-like texture that meets Castelvetrano olives and Marcona almonds.
value.sayIt: With the papillote, Raúl Pérez Ultreia Godello from Bierzo: textured and saline, great with olives and almonds.

classic.why: Salt and acid: Santorini Assyrtiko has salty, lemony acidity for olives and tomato and steamed fish.
classic.sayIt: For a bottle, Gai’a Assyrtiko from Santorini: bone dry, salty and lemony, perfect with the fish and olives.

splurge.why: Bridge and weight: Trévallon blanc has Provençal herbs and texture that echo olives, tomato and banana leaf.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Domaine de Trévallon white from Provence: rare, herbal and rich, lovely with the papillote.

value.why: Fat and acid: Sanford and Benedict Chardonnay has richness for mustard cream and acidity for the fried crust.
value.sayIt: With the hen, Au Bon Climat Sanford and Benedict Chardonnay: rich and fresh, lovely with mustard cream.

classic.why: Fat and weight: Meursault has the creamy richness that mirrors mustard cream, with acidity for the fried skin.
classic.sayIt: For a bottle, Bitouzet-Prieur Meursault Les Corbins: creamy white Burgundy, classic with a mustard cream sauce.

splurge.why: Fat and salt: vintage Blanc de Blancs Champagne cuts the fried crust and mustard cream, and its chalky freshness keeps each bite light.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Pol Roger Blanc de Blancs: vintage Champagne with a fried hen, rich, crisp and celebratory.

half.why: Fat and salt: a half of Blanc de Blancs sparkling cuts fried skin and cream sauce.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Schramsberg Blanc de Blancs: crisp California bubbles, great with the fried hen.

value.why: Bridge and heat: Willamette Pinot Noir has earthy fruit for shiitakes and low tannin that stays calm with blackening spice.
value.sayIt: With the blackened tofu, Ken Wright Willamette Valley Pinot Noir: earthy and silky, lovely with the mushrooms.

classic.why: Bridge and salt: a Nuits-Saint-Georges with age shows savory, mushroom notes that echo preserved shiitake.
classic.sayIt: For a bottle, Grivot Nuits-Saint-Georges Les Charmois: savory red Burgundy with age, beautiful with shiitakes.

splurge.why: Bridge and weight: Roumier Morey-Saint-Denis Premier Cru has earthy depth and silk for umami mushrooms and rice grits.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Georges Roumier Clos de la Bussière: a red Burgundy from a legendary grower, earthy and silky.

half.why: Bridge: a half of Oregon Pinot Noir gives earthy red fruit for mushrooms in a lighter pour.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Bergstrom Reserve Pinot Noir: earthy and bright, a nice match for the tofu.

value.why: Heat and weight: Zinfandel has ripe fruit and soft tannin that handle chili crisp and Creole spice.
value.sayIt: With the Creole hanger steak, Ridge Three Valleys Zinfandel: ripe, spicy and juicy, great with chili crisp.

classic.why: Heat and bridge: Lytton Springs has brambly fruit and spice that meet Creole seasoning and Madeira glaze.
classic.sayIt: For a bottle, Ridge Lytton Springs: a Zinfandel blend, spicy and generous, made for this steak.

splurge.why: Weight and heat: Vieux Télégraphe with age has Grenache warmth and soft tannin for spicy beef and persillade.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Vieux Télégraphe Châteauneuf-du-Pape with age: savory, spicy and silky with the steak.

half.why: Heat: a half of Lytton Springs gives ripe fruit for spice in a two glass pour.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Ridge Lytton Springs: spicy, ripe Zinfandel, perfect with the steak.

value.why: Sweet and acid: a mature Nahe Spätlese has honeyed fruit for banana and caramel and acidity to cut the butter.
value.sayIt: With Bananas Foster, a Hexamer Riesling Spätlese with age: honeyed and bright, lovely with caramelized banana.

classic.why: Bridge and sweet: an old Rivesaltes is sweet fortified wine with caramel and nut notes that echo the flambéed sauce.
classic.sayIt: For something special, a 1975 Rivesaltes from Roussillon: an old sweet wine, caramel and nuts, made for Foster.

splurge.why: Sweet and bridge: an old Sauternes has crème brûlée and caramel depth for the butter, brown sugar and rum.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Château Gilette Crème de Tête: a rare, long aged Sauternes, caramel and apricot with the bananas.

half.why: Sweet: a late harvest half is honeyed enough for caramel sauce and vanilla ice cream.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Grgich Hills Violetta, a late harvest Napa dessert wine: honeyed and lovely with Foster.

value.why: Bridge and sweet: Late Bottled Vintage Port has dark cherry fruit and sweetness for black cherries and Luxardo sauce.
value.sayIt: With Cherries Jubilee, a Sandeman Late Bottled Vintage Port: dark cherry and spice, perfect with the sauce.

classic.why: Bridge and tannin: a mature single quinta vintage Port has cherry and spice with softened tannin for the ice cream.
classic.sayIt: For something special, Taylor Fladgate Quinta de Vargellas with age: mellow vintage Port, cherries and spice.

splurge.why: Bridge and sweet: a 1977 Taylor Fladgate vintage Port has dried cherry and spice that match the flambéed fruit.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Taylor Fladgate 1977 vintage Port: almost fifty years old, silky and spiced, glorious with cherries.

half.why: Bridge: a half of sweet Zinfandel tastes of ripe dark cherry, echoing the dessert.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Ridge Essence, a sweet Zinfandel: ripe cherry and spice, fun with the jubilee.

value.why: Sweet and bridge: twenty-year-old sweet Chenin is as sweet as the whiskey caramel, with honey and quince for the pralines and acidity for the custard.
value.sayIt: With the bread pudding, Baumard’s sweet Loire Chenin: honey, quince and baked apple, sweet enough for the caramel and bright to finish.
value.note: Re-chosen by the repairer, 4 October 2026: Barbadillo Pale Cream is a lightly sweetened fino and tastes thin beside whiskey caramel.

classic.why: Sweet and acid: Sauternes has honeyed apricot for the caramel and acidity to lift the custard.
classic.sayIt: For a bottle, Château Suduiraut Sauternes: honey and apricot, classic with bread pudding.

splurge.why: Sweet and fat: Yquem has the sweetness and richness for custard and whiskey caramel, with acidity to keep it lively.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Château d’Yquem: the world’s most famous Sauternes, honeyed and luminous with bread pudding.

half.why: Sweet: a half of Sauternes gives honey and apricot for caramel in a two glass pour.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Château Suduiraut Sauternes: honeyed and golden, made for bread pudding.

value.why: Sweet and bridge: Late Bottled Vintage Port has dark fruit and cocoa notes that match milk chocolate and caramel.
value.sayIt: With the Snickers, a Late Bottled Vintage Port from Feist: chocolatey and rich, great with caramel and peanuts.

classic.why: Sweet and tannin: vintage Port has ripe fruit and grip for milk chocolate, caramel custard and roasted peanuts.
classic.sayIt: For something special, Graham’s 2000 vintage Port: rich, ripe and chocolatey, made for this dessert.

splurge.why: Sweet and bridge: a 1983 Graham’s vintage Port has mellowed into nutty, dried fruit depth for nougat and peanuts.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Graham’s 1983 vintage Port: over forty years old, mellow and nutty with chocolate.

half.why: Sweet: a half of vintage Port gives rich fruit for chocolate in a smaller pour.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Dow’s 2000 vintage Port: rich and dark, perfect with chocolate.

value.why: Sweet and acid: a Goldkapsel Spätlese is sweet with piercing acidity, one of the few wines that survives lemon.
value.sayIt: With the lemon tart, a sweet Mosel Riesling from Dr. Hermann: bright and honeyed, it keeps up with the lemon.

classic.why: Sweet and acid: Barsac is known for freshness among sweet Bordeaux, with citrus notes for yuzu and meringue.
classic.sayIt: For a bottle, Château Climens from Barsac: sweet but fresh, with citrus notes, lovely with lemon and yuzu.

splurge.why: Sweet and acid: Yquem has the sweetness to stay above lemon jelly and the acidity to stay fresh.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, a half-bottle of Château d’Yquem: honeyed and bright, extraordinary with the lemon tart.

half.why: Sweet and acid: a Goldkapsel Auslese half has the sweetness and acidity to match lemon and yuzu.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Dönhoff Oberhäuser Brücke Auslese: sweet, racy Riesling, made for lemon desserts.

value.why: Sweet and bridge: late harvest Moscadello has honeyed, tropical fruit for charred pineapple and caramel.
value.sayIt: With the tarte Tatin, Banfi Florus, a late harvest Moscadello: honeyed and fruity, lovely with pineapple.

classic.why: Sweet and bridge: a Kracher Auslese has honeyed, tropical richness for charred pineapple and sweet anglaise.
classic.sayIt: For a bottle, Alois Kracher Auslese from Austria: rich, honeyed and tropical, made for pineapple and caramel.

splurge.why: Sweet and acid: a magnum of JJ Prüm Goldkapsel Auslese brings tropical honey and racy acidity for a table sharing dessert.
splurge.sayIt: For a table celebrating, a magnum of JJ Prüm Auslese: sweet, racy Mosel Riesling, gorgeous with pineapple.

half.why: Sweet and acid: Keller PIUS Auslese half has honeyed fruit and acidity for caramel and pineapple.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Keller PIUS Auslese: sweet, pure Riesling from a great grower, lovely with the tatin.

value.why: Salt and heat: Tasmanian sparkling has bright bubbles that refresh after salt and Creole spice.
value.sayIt: With the spiced nuts, Jansz from Tasmania: crisp sparkling wine, perfect for snacking.

classic.why: Salt and bridge: Charles Heidsieck Réserve has toasty, nutty richness that echoes roasted nuts and tames spice.
classic.sayIt: For a bottle of Champagne, Charles Heidsieck Réserve: rich and toasty, lovely with spiced nuts.

splurge.why: Salt and bridge: Krug Grande Cuvée has toasted nut and brioche depth that meets roasted spiced nuts.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Krug Grande Cuvée: the great multi vintage Champagne, rich, nutty and layered.

half.why: Salt: a half of grower Brut gives two glasses of bubbles for a salty snack.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Tribaut-Schloesser Brut: easy, crisp Champagne for two with the nuts.

value.why: Fat and acid: Trento rosé sparkling cuts fried pastry and rémoulade, with red fruit for crawfish.
value.sayIt: With the meat pies, Ferrari rosé from Trento: crisp Italian sparkling, lovely with fried pastry.

classic.why: Fat and salt: Billecart-Salmon Réserve is bright and fine, made to cut fried pastry and creamy rémoulade.
classic.sayIt: For a bottle of Champagne, Billecart-Salmon Réserve: elegant and fresh, perfect with crawfish pies.

splurge.why: Weight and fat: Bollinger La Grande Année has the depth for crawfish and the acidity for rich pastry.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Bollinger La Grande Année: rich vintage Champagne, superb with crawfish pies.

half.why: Fat: a half of Trento Brut gives bubbles for fried pastry in a two glass pour.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Ferrari Brut: crisp Italian sparkling, great with the pies.

value.why: Acid and fat: pétillant Vouvray has the acidity for pickles and gentle bubbles for frying and chive cream.
value.sayIt: With fried pickles, Huet Pétillant from Vouvray: lightly sparkling Chenin, bright and fun with the pickles.

classic.why: Acid and fat: Extra Brut grower Champagne is dry enough for vinegar and fresh enough for fried batter.
classic.sayIt: For a bottle, JM Sélèque Solessence Extra Brut: a grower Champagne, crisp and dry, great with fried pickles.

splurge.why: Acid and salt: Selosse Initial has vivid acidity and depth that turn a fried snack into an occasion.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Jacques Selosse Initial: a cult grower Champagne, intense and unforgettable.

half.why: Acid: a half of Blanc de Blancs Extra Brut gives crisp acidity for pickles and batter.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Veuve Fourny Blanc de Blancs: bone dry Champagne for the pickles.

value.why: Heat and fat: Trento rosé sparkling cools Crystal gastrique and cuts fried shrimp.
value.sayIt: With popcorn shrimp, Cesarini Sforza rosé from Trento: crisp, fruity bubbles, great with hot sauce.

classic.why: Fat and heat: Roederer Collection 244 is fresh and fine, cutting fried shrimp and soothing hot sauce.
classic.sayIt: For a bottle of Champagne, Louis Roederer Collection 244: fresh, fine and lovely with fried shrimp.

splurge.why: Fat and acid: Cristal has precision and depth that cut fried batter and make a snack a celebration.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Louis Roederer Cristal: one of the most famous Champagnes in the world, precise and elegant.

value.why: Sweet and salt: Late Bottled Vintage Port has sweet fruit that meets salty cheese and chutney.
value.sayIt: With the cheese board, Sandeman Late Bottled Vintage Port: sweet, dark fruit, classic with cheese.

classic.why: Sweet and acid: an aged demi-sec Vouvray has honeyed sweetness for cheese and honey, with acidity to cut richness.
classic.sayIt: For a bottle, Huet Clos du Bourg demi-sec with age: honeyed Chenin, wonderful with cheese and honey.

splurge.why: Sweet and salt: a 1985 Dow’s vintage Port has mellow sweetness for salty cheese and fruit and nut bread.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Dow’s 1985 vintage Port: over forty years old, mellow and complex, perfect with cheese.

half.why: Sweet and salt: an Auslese half has honeyed sweetness and acidity for salty cheese and honey.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Dönhoff Auslese: honeyed Riesling, lovely with cheese and Brennan’s honey.

value.why: Tannin and fat: Rioja Crianza has soft tannin and savory fruit for short rib patties, bacon and cheese.
value.sayIt: With the burger, López de Heredia Cubillo Rioja: savory, mellow Tempranillo, great with beef and bacon.

classic.why: Tannin and fat: ripe Napa Cabernet has plush fruit and structure for beef, cheese and tomato jam.
classic.sayIt: For a bottle, Caymus Napa Valley Cabernet: rich and plush, a favorite with a great burger.

splurge.why: Tannin and weight: Silver Oak Napa Cabernet has ripe structure for double short rib patties and bacon.
splurge.sayIt: For a celebration, Silver Oak Napa Valley Cabernet: a guest favorite, polished and generous with beef.

half.why: Fat: a half of Napa Merlot gives soft, plush fruit for beef and cheese.
half.sayIt: A half-bottle of Duckhorn Merlot: soft and plush, an easy match for the burger.
